analysis: The PR adds a manual-dispatch CI workflow (.github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml) that rebuilds a re-quantized model, verifies it byte for byte against a dispatcher-supplied manifest, and uploads it to the darkbloom-models R2 bucket. It also adds scripts/models tooling and tests, a ci-master test step, docs, and a UNROUTED entry in test-darkbloom-route.py. No provider runtime, coordinator, attestation, App Attest or cache code (TB-002/009/011, T-041) is touched. The relevant surface is the model-weight supply chain (A-004, T-012, T-027). Workflow controls verified in the replayed YAML: inputs reach scripts only through env; a secret-free preflight job runs first; the checkout is SHA-pinned with persist-credentials false; permissions are contents:read; pip installs use --require-hashes --only-binary; secrets appear only in the check step and the upload step; the check prints only a verdict; the upload requires this run's check to have passed for the chosen key set; and the job runs in the `prod` environment. Adding the workflow to UNROUTED forces literal Blacksmith runners, which tightens the CI guard. Not verifiable from supplied evidence, so not findings: (1) the in-file master ref guard cannot stop a copy of the workflow on a `v*` branch, so the `prod` environment's reviewer and branch policy is the real control; the file notes this as a pending owner action. (2) The repository-level legacy R2_* key is a broad bucket credential readable by any workflow a writer pushes; the file documents this. (3) upload-model-revision.py, publish-model-revision.py, the hash values in requirements-requant-upload.txt, and the unit tests were reviewed only through other passes' analyses. The manifest comparison is the integrity anchor. Its provenance is the dispatcher, and approval covers the deployment. The threat model may later need an entry for this CI publication path and R2 credential custody.

findings.detail: Two source passes report that cmd_build in scripts/models/requant.py (about lines 401-410) fetches the template's manifest.json and writes each non-model entry to os.path.join(out, path) without rejecting absolute paths, '..' segments or separators, and without checking the entry's sha256. I could not replay requant.py in this pass, so the line number and behavior come from those passes. If the template were tampered with or mistaken, the build could write outside the output directory on the runner. In the prod-environment job, $RUNNER_TEMP holds manifest.json and the hash-pinned venv at tools/bin, which is on PATH. An overwrite of tools/bin/* or manifest.json could therefore execute attacker-chosen code in the later upload step, which holds R2 write credentials. The workflow validates template_url as a models.darkbloom.ai URL under the model's own prefix, but not the manifest contents it points to. Fix: accept only plain relative paths, resolve each under out and assert containment, verify size and sha256 before writing, and restrict get() to https.
findings.title: requant.py build writes template-manifest paths to disk without containment or scheme checks
